title: XSS Prevention
definition: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a vulnerability where attackers inject malicious JavaScript into web pages viewed by other users. React automatically protects against most XSS attacks by escaping string variables in JSX.
simpleExplanation:
If someone fills out a comment form and types ``, an unsafe website might literally print that to the screen, causing the browser to execute it. React is smart. If you try to render that comment inside a `
{comment}
`, React converts the `<` and `>` into safe text characters (`<` and `>`). It displays the code as harmless text, rather than executing it.
realWorldExample: A user updates their profile name to ``. In React, this safely renders as text on the screen. In raw jQuery or vanilla `innerHTML`, this would pop up an alert box.
useCases: Protecting the application from malicious input

answers.question: How do attackers steal data?
answers.answer: They use injected JavaScript to read `document.cookie` (stealing your session token) or `localStorage`, and then send that data to their own server using `fetch()`. They can then log in as you.
